correctness.rationale: For a t-row team the number of nonconstant alphabet words is exactly m^t-m, yielding a necessary lower bound on t. Distinct chosen words and distinct chosen constant labels realize every compatible equality–constancy type; duplicate rows would contradict t minimality. Restricting m constant functions and r genuine nonconstant coordinate functions to selected rows starts with m singleton value classes and increases the class count at most r times. Staircase profiles require all r+1 rows. Weak-negation formulas force k distinct nonconstant columns and attain the bound, and the published Lemma 3.3 proves equivalence of all empty-signature FOT-minus formulas. Exhaustive finite testing checked initial alphabets/arities independently.

value.rationale: For a recently isolated logically complete type invariant, the exact minimal size of any representative is logarithmic in the number of distinct nonconstant free-variable columns, whereas the smallest guaranteed subteam of given data can be linear; the exact two resource costs and sharp formula witnesses matter for compressing and constructing examples, bound-preserving logical reasoning, and understanding the distinction between fresh models and data sparsification. This is a natural parameter attached to complete types, not an arbitrary census.
